question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

Writing habit is a good and easily exercise for the brain.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. good and easily exercise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Exercise” is a noun here, and a noun must be modified by an adjective, never by an adverb.

◦ “Easily” is an adverb (सरलता से); the adjective form is easy (आसान). Since “good” (adjective) and the second word are joined by “and”, both must belong to the same class.

◦ Correct: Writing habit is a good and easy exercise for the brain.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “for the brain.” is correct — preposition “for” + noun phrase.

• Option 3 “Writing habit is a” is correct — singular subject with singular verb “is” and article “a”.

• Option 4 “No error” is wrong because the adverb “easily” is clearly misused for the adjective “easy”.

NOTE

• Adjective modifies a noun; adverb modifies a verb/adjective/adverb: “He is a quick learner” but “He learns quickly”.

• Frequently tested adjective–adverb pairs: easy/easily, hard/hardly, late/lately, near/nearly, high/highly.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Most impressive / was record breaking / 75.6 FPS on Crysis.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. was record breaking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase needs the indefinite article “a” before the singular countable noun phrase “record-breaking 75.6 FPS”, and “record-breaking” must work as a single compound adjective.

◦ An article is compulsory before a singular countable noun that is being mentioned for the first time. (अनिश्चित उपपद)

◦ Correct: Most impressive was a record-breaking 75.6 FPS on Crysis.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “75.6 FPS on Crysis.” is fine — the figure with the preposition “on” and the game’s name is correctly used.

• Option 2 “Most impressive” is a correct fronted complement of the sentence.

• Option 4 “No error” is wrong because the article is missing in segment 3.

NOTE

• Compound adjectives placed before a noun are hyphenated: record-breaking performance, well-known author, ten-year-old boy.

• Numbers/measurements still take an article when used as a countable noun: “a 40% rise”, “an 8-hour shift”.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Instead of the sweet taste she expected, it was ______ - like alum
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. bitter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bitter means having a sharp, unpleasant taste, the opposite of sweet. (कड़वा)

◦ The sentence sets up a contrast with “Instead of the sweet taste she expected”, so the blank must carry the sense opposite to “sweet”.

◦ Alum (फिटकरी) is famously astringent and bitter, which confirms the choice.

◦ Correct: Instead of the sweet taste she expected, it was bitter - like alum.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Dulcet — sweet and soothing, usually of sound (मधुर); it would repeat, not contrast with, “sweet”.

• Aromatic — having a pleasant, distinctive smell (सुगंधित); it describes smell, not the contrast in taste.

• Tenacious — holding on firmly, persistent (दृढ़); unrelated to taste.

NOTE

• Taste vocabulary for SSC: sour (खट्टा), pungent (तीखा), bland/insipid (फीका), savoury (नमकीन), acrid (कड़वा-तीखा).

• Contrast markers such as “instead of”, “rather than”, “on the contrary” signal that an opposite word fits the blank.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

What should I doing if the power goes out?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. should I do.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A modal auxiliary (should, would, can, may, must) is always followed by the bare infinitive (V1), never by V-ing or V3. (सहायक क्रिया के बाद मूल क्रिया)

◦ In an interrogative sentence the pattern is: Wh-word + modal + subject + V1 → “What should I do…?”

◦ The “if” clause is in the simple present (“goes out”), which suits a first-conditional style question about the future.

◦ Correct: What should I do if the power goes out?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “shall I does” is wrong — a modal can never take “does”, and “shall” with “I” would change the sense to an offer.

• Option 2 “No improvement” is wrong because “should I doing” is ungrammatical.

• Option 4 “should I had done” is wrong — the correct perfect modal form would be “should I have done”, which also changes the tense wrongly.

NOTE

• Modal + V1: “She can swim”, “He must go”, “You may leave”.

• Modal + have + V3 expresses past speculation/regret: “I should have gone”, “She must have forgotten”.

question:
Select the word from the options which is similar in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

He is interested in how our (perceptions) of death affect the way we live.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. approaches.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Perception means the way in which something is regarded, understood or interpreted. (धारणा, दृष्टिकोण)

◦ Approach here carries the sense of a particular way of viewing or dealing with something, which is the closest available match for “ways of regarding death”.

◦ Correct: He is interested in how our approaches to death affect the way we live.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ignorance — lack of knowledge (अज्ञानता); it is the absence of understanding, not a way of understanding.

• Bewilderment — a state of confusion (घबराहट); it names an emotion, not a viewpoint.

• Misconception — a wrong or mistaken idea (भ्रांति); “perception” is neutral and need not be wrong.

NOTE

• Closer one-word synonyms of perception: outlook, viewpoint, notion, impression, understanding.

• Remember the pair: perception (धारणा) vs deception (धोखा) vs conception (कल्पना/धारणा का बनना).

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

The room beneath the collapsed building was empty.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. mended.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Collapsed means fallen down or caved in suddenly. (ढह गया)

◦ Mended means repaired or put back into good condition (मरम्मत किया हुआ), which is the direct opposite of a structure that has fallen apart.

◦ Correct: The opposite of a collapsed building is a mended (repaired) building.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Finished — completed or ended (समाप्त); it refers to completion, not to repair, so it is not an antonym.

• Cracked — split or broken (चटका हुआ); this is a synonym-side word, close in sense to collapsed.

• Choked — blocked or unable to breathe (अवरुद्ध); unrelated to a building’s structural state.

NOTE

• Synonyms of collapse: crumble, cave in, give way, disintegrate, topple.

• Antonyms of collapse: build, erect, construct, strengthen, restore.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

I began with writing one a week and now I do so every day.
option_3: now I do so every day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. one a week and.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence needs the adverb of frequency “once”, not the numeral “one”. “Once a week” means one time in a week. (सप्ताह में एक बार)

◦ Frequency is expressed as: once a week, twice a month, thrice a year, and it contrasts naturally with “every day” later in the sentence.

◦ Correct: I began with writing once a week and now I do so every day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 “I began with writing” is acceptable — “begin with” + gerund shows the starting point of a habit.

• Option 3 “now I do so every day.” is correct — “do so” substitutes for the earlier verb phrase.

• Option 4 “No error” is wrong because “one a week” must be “once a week”.

NOTE

• Numeral vs frequency adverb: one → once, two → twice, three → thrice/three times.

• After “begin/start”, both gerund and infinitive are possible: “She began singing” = “She began to sing”.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

They will took their grandchildren to the zoo.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. took their.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Will” is a modal and must be followed by the bare infinitive (V1), so “will took” (modal + V2) is ungrammatical.

◦ Among the given choices, the only grammatically complete verb phrase is the simple past “took”, which fits a completed action. (भूतकाल)

◦ Correct: They took their grandchildren to the zoo.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “No improvement” is wrong because “will took” breaks the modal + V1 rule.

• Option 2 “taken their” is wrong — “taken” (V3) needs an auxiliary such as “have/had/were” before it.

• Option 3 “takes their” is wrong — the plural subject “They” takes the base verb “take”, not “takes”.

NOTE

• Verb forms of take: take – took – taken; of go: go – went – gone; of write: write – wrote – written.

• Modal + V1 always: “will go”, “can do”, “must see”; never “will went”, “can did”.

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Curious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Uninterested.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Curious means eager to know or learn something; inquisitive. (जिज्ञासु)

◦ Uninterested means not interested, showing no eagerness to know (उदासीन), which is the exact opposite of curiosity.

◦ Correct: A curious student asks questions, whereas an uninterested student asks none.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Passionate — showing strong feeling or enthusiasm (उत्साही); it is closer in spirit to curious, not opposite.

• Doubtful — uncertain, having doubts (संदेहपूर्ण); doubt is not the opposite of curiosity.

• Complex — complicated, having many parts (जटिल); it describes things, not attitude.

NOTE

• Synonyms of curious: inquisitive, prying, interested, questioning, nosy.

• Do not confuse uninterested (not interested) with disinterested (impartial, unbiased) — a very common SSC trap.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

When we reached my room, I couldn’t ______ back my smile.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. hold.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb “hold back” means to restrain or suppress an emotion. (रोकना, दबाना)

◦ “Couldn’t” is a modal (could + not), and a modal is always followed by the bare infinitive V1, so only “hold” can follow.

◦ Correct: When we reached my room, I couldn’t hold back my smile.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 “squeeze” is V1 but “squeeze back” is not an idiomatic phrasal verb for suppressing a smile.

• Option 3 “held” is the past form (V2) and cannot follow the modal “couldn’t”.

• Option 4 “kept” is also V2, and “keep back a smile” is not the standard collocation.

NOTE

• Common “hold” phrasal verbs: hold back (restrain), hold on (wait), hold up (delay/rob), hold out (resist).

• Emotions collocate with: hold back tears, choke back sobs, fight back tears, suppress a laugh.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

They were ______ there when Janvi heard something large and heavy collide with the door.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. almost.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Almost is an adverb meaning “nearly, very close to but not completely”. (लगभग)

◦ “They were almost there” is a fixed, idiomatic expression meaning they had nearly reached the destination, which suits the sudden interruption described.

◦ Correct: They were almost there when Janvi heard something large and heavy collide with the door.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Much is used with uncountable nouns or comparatives (“much better”), not before “there”.

• Most is a superlative/quantifier (“most people”, “most beautiful”) and does not fit an adverb slot before “there”.

• About can mean “approximately”, but it precedes numbers or quantities (“about ten minutes”), not the adverb “there”.

NOTE

• Almost + there/all/everyone/never: “almost every day”, “almost never”.

• Distinguish almost (nearly) from mostly (mainly) and at most (maximum).

question: Select the wrongly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Anarcy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is ANARCHY, with the letters c-h-y at the end; the option drops the “h”.

◦ Anarchy means a state of disorder due to the absence of authority or government. (अराजकता)

◦ Correct: The country slipped into complete anarchy after the coup.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Adverse (प्रतिकूल) — unfavourable or harmful; correctly spelt.

• Annul (रद्द करना) — to declare invalid, especially a marriage or law; correctly spelt with double “n”.

• Adulterate (मिलावट करना) — to make impure by adding an inferior substance; correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words from Greek “arche” (rule): anarchy, monarchy, oligarchy, hierarchy — all keep -archy.

• Do not confuse adverse (unfavourable) with averse (unwilling, opposed to).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

For better or (for) worse
option_4: To accept whatever results; good or bad
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To accept whatever results; good or bad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom “for better or (for) worse” means whatever the consequences may be — good or bad — one accepts the situation. (जो भी परिणाम हो, अच्छा या बुरा)

◦ It comes from the traditional marriage vow “for better, for worse”, indicating unconditional acceptance.

◦ Correct: For better or for worse, we have decided to shift to a new city.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• “Become out of control” is expressed by idioms like get out of hand or run riot.

• “Extreme enthusiasm” matches gung-ho or full of beans.

• “To be in trouble” matches in hot water or in a fix.

NOTE

• Related idioms: come what may (whatever happens), take the rough with the smooth, through thick and thin (in all circumstances).

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Disappointed and annoyed about something
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Disgruntled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Disgruntled means angry, dissatisfied or discontented, especially because one’s expectations were not met. (असंतुष्ट, नाराज़)

◦ It combines exactly the two ideas in the clue — disappointment and annoyance.

◦ Correct: The disgruntled employees refused to attend the meeting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Contented (संतुष्ट) — happy and satisfied; it is the opposite of the required meaning.

• Dissuade (मना करना) — to persuade someone not to do something; it is a verb, not an adjective describing mood.

• Surreal (अवास्तविक) — strange and dreamlike, unreal; unrelated to emotion of annoyance.

NOTE

• Synonyms of disgruntled: aggrieved, resentful, discontented, peeved, sulky.

• Antonyms: pleased, satisfied, gratified, contented.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

To move about from place to place aimlessly
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Meander.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Meander means to wander aimlessly, or (of a river) to follow a winding course. (लक्ष्यहीन घूमना, टेढ़ा-मेढ़ा बहना)

◦ The key idea in the clue is aimless movement, which only “meander” conveys.

◦ Correct: We spent the afternoon meandering through the narrow lanes of the old city.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Meadow (चारागाह) — a field of grass, a noun denoting a place, not an action.

• Path (रास्ता) — a track or way; again a noun, and it implies a fixed route, not aimlessness.

• Stream (धारा) — a small river; it names a water body rather than aimless movement.

NOTE

• Synonyms of meander: ramble, roam, wander, saunter, stroll, drift.

• Note the geography use too: a meander is a bend in a river; an abandoned meander forms an oxbow lake.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Long in the tooth
option_1: The show has come to an end
option_2: Be optimistic, even difficult times will lead to better days
option_3: To be old, often too old to do something
option_4: Killing of a certain ethnic or religious group on a massive scale
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To be old, often too old to do something.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom “long in the tooth” means rather old, past one’s prime. (बूढ़ा होना)

◦ It comes from horse-trading: a horse’s gums recede with age, so its teeth appear longer — hence age is judged by the teeth.

◦ Correct: He is a bit long in the tooth to be playing professional cricket now.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• “The show has come to an end” corresponds to the curtain falls or that’s all she wrote.

• “Be optimistic, even difficult times will lead to better days” corresponds to every cloud has a silver lining.

• “Killing of a certain ethnic or religious group on a massive scale” is the word genocide, not an idiom.

NOTE

• Other age idioms: over the hill (past one’s best), no spring chicken (not young), getting on in years.

• Related horse idiom: don’t look a gift horse in the mouth — do not question the value of a gift.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

“What ______ your dad do at the Ministry of Magic, anyway?”
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. does.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is a simple present interrogative asking about a habitual activity (a job), so the auxiliary do/does is needed with the main verb “do”.

◦ The subject “your dad” is third person singular, and in the simple present the singular subject takes does. (एकवचन कर्ता के साथ does)

◦ Correct: “What does your dad do at the Ministry of Magic, anyway?”

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “is” is wrong — “is … do” is impossible; “is doing” would be needed, which changes the structure.

• Option 2 “have” is wrong — the perfect tense would require “has done”, not “have … do”.

• Option 4 “do” is wrong — “do” is used with I/we/you/they and plural subjects, not with a singular subject like “your dad”.

NOTE

• Simple present question pattern: Wh-word + do/does + subject + V1.

• Once “does/did” is used, the main verb stays in the base form: “What did he say?”, not “What did he said?”.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Advocate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Support.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Advocate (verb) means to publicly recommend or support a particular cause or policy; as a noun it means a person who pleads for a cause. (समर्थन करना; वकील)

◦ “Support” carries the same core sense of backing or speaking in favour of something.

◦ Correct: Many scientists advocate (= support) stricter limits on carbon emissions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Justice (न्याय) — fairness or the legal system; it is related to the courtroom sense but is not a synonym of the word itself.

• Forever (हमेशा के लिए) — an adverb of time; completely unrelated in meaning.

• Experience (अनुभव) — knowledge gained through practice; unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of advocate: champion, endorse, uphold, promote, back, espouse.

• Antonyms of advocate: oppose, resist, discourage, denounce, impugn.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘no substitution required’.

(The people of Philippines has voted) to elect a new president.
option_2: The people of Philippines have voted
option_3: The people of the Philippines have voted
option_4: The people of the Philippines has voted
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The people of the Philippines have voted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two corrections are needed together. First, the definite article “the” is compulsory before the names of countries that are plural in form or a group of islands: the Philippines, the Netherlands, the Maldives, the USA.

◦ Second, the noun “people” in the sense of “persons” is plural, so it takes the plural verb have, not “has”. (लोग — बहुवचन)

◦ Correct: The people of the Philippines have voted to elect a new president.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong because the printed segment has two errors — a missing article and a wrong verb.

• Option 2 fixes the verb but still omits “the” before Philippines.

• Option 4 supplies the article but keeps the singular verb “has”, which does not agree with “people”.

NOTE

• “The” with countries: the Philippines, the Netherlands, the UAE, the UK; but no article with India, China, Japan.

• “People” = persons (plural verb); “peoples” = communities/nations, as in “the peoples of Asia”.

question: Four words are given, out of which only one word is spelt correctly. Choose the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. PRESENCE.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• PRESENCE is spelt correctly — p-r-e-s-e-n-c-e. It means the state of being present or a person’s bearing. (उपस्थिति)

◦ Correct: Your presence at the meeting is mandatory.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “CAMOFLAGUE” is wrong; the correct spelling is CAMOUFLAGE (छद्मावरण) — hiding by blending with the surroundings.

• Option 2 “COMPARSION” is wrong; the correct spelling is COMPARISON (तुलना), formed from “compare” + “-ison”.

• Option 3 “GUAGE” is wrong; the correct spelling is GAUGE (मापक) — to measure, or an instrument for measuring.

NOTE

• Note the noun–adjective pair: presence → present; absence → absent.

• Other commonly misspelt SSC words: occurrence, maintenance, embarrass, harass, questionnaire, liaison.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Body language (1) ______ ideas or thoughts by certain actions, either intentionally or unintentionally. A (2) ______ can be a way of flirting or indicating that the party is only joking . A (3) ______ signifies approval, while (4) ______ of the head indicates a negative reaction. Other forms of non (5) ______ language can be found in Braille (a system of raised dots read with the fingertips), signal flags, Morse code, and smoke signals..

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. transmits.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Transmit means to pass on, send or communicate something from one person or place to another. (संप्रेषित करना)

◦ The subject “Body language” is singular, so the singular present verb transmits is required, and the object “ideas or thoughts” shows that communication is meant.

◦ Correct: Body language transmits ideas or thoughts by certain actions, either intentionally or unintentionally.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Delimit — to fix the limits or boundaries of something (परिसीमन करना); it does not mean to convey.

• Intermit — to stop or suspend temporarily; it is rare and gives the opposite idea of continuous conveying.

• Retransmit — to transmit again; nothing in the passage suggests repetition of an earlier message.

NOTE

• Words from Latin “mittere” (to send): transmit, emit, submit, admit, remit, omit.

• Collocations: transmit a signal/disease/message/knowledge.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Body language (1) ______ ideas or thoughts by certain actions, either intentionally or unintentionally. A (2) ______ can be a way of flirting or indicating that the party is only joking . A (3) ______ signifies approval, while (4) ______ of the head indicates a negative reaction. Other forms of non (5) ______ language can be found in Braille (a system of raised dots read with the fingertips), signal flags, Morse code, and smoke signals..

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. wink.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A wink is the closing and opening of one eye quickly, used as a private signal. (आँख मारना)

◦ The passage says the gesture “can be a way of flirting or indicating that the party is only joking” — both are classic functions of a wink.

◦ Correct: A wink can be a way of flirting or indicating that the party is only joking.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nod — to move the head up and down; it signals agreement, and the passage assigns approval to blank 3.

• Shake — a side-to-side head movement signalling refusal, which the passage assigns to blank 4.

• Clap — striking the palms together to applaud; it expresses appreciation, not flirtation or joking.

NOTE

• Gesture vocabulary: shrug (indifference), beckon (call closer), wave (greeting/farewell), frown (displeasure).

• Idiom: a nod is as good as a wink — a hint is enough for someone who understands.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Body language (1) ______ ideas or thoughts by certain actions, either intentionally or unintentionally. A (2) ______ can be a way of flirting or indicating that the party is only joking . A (3) ______ signifies approval, while (4) ______ of the head indicates a negative reaction. Other forms of non (5) ______ language can be found in Braille (a system of raised dots read with the fingertips), signal flags, Morse code, and smoke signals..

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. nod.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A nod is a short up-and-down movement of the head that universally signals yes, agreement or approval. (सिर हिलाकर सहमति देना)

◦ The blank is followed by “signifies approval”, and it is contrasted with the next blank, which “indicates a negative reaction”.

◦ Correct: A nod signifies approval, while a shake of the head indicates a negative reaction.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Shake (of the head) conveys disapproval or refusal — that is the contrast word needed in blank 4, not here.

• Wink conveys flirtation or a shared joke and has already been used in blank 2.

• Clap shows applause or appreciation, which is not the same as signifying approval of a statement.

NOTE

• Useful phrases: nod off (fall asleep), give the nod (approve/select), on the nod (approved without discussion).

• Contrast pairs in cloze passages are signalled by connectors such as while, whereas, but, on the other hand.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Body language (1) ______ ideas or thoughts by certain actions, either intentionally or unintentionally. A (2) ______ can be a way of flirting or indicating that the party is only joking . A (3) ______ signifies approval, while (4) ______ of the head indicates a negative reaction. Other forms of non (5) ______ language can be found in Braille (a system of raised dots read with the fingertips), signal flags, Morse code, and smoke signals..

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. shake.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A shake of the head is a side-to-side movement that signals no, refusal or disapproval. (सिर हिलाकर मना करना)

◦ The blank is immediately followed by “of the head indicates a negative reaction”, and the connector “while” demands a contrast with the approving “nod” in blank 3.

◦ Correct: A nod signifies approval, while a shake of the head indicates a negative reaction.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Clap — applause with the hands; one does not “clap of the head”, so it fails the collocation test.

• Wink — an eye gesture already used for flirting/joking in blank 2.

• Nod — signals approval, the positive gesture used in blank 3, hence the opposite of what is needed.

NOTE

• Collocation clue: only nod and shake combine with “of the head”; the phrase after the blank often decides the answer in cloze tests.

• Related expressions: shake hands (greet), shake off (get rid of), shake up (reorganise/shock).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Body language (1) ______ ideas or thoughts by certain actions, either intentionally or unintentionally. A (2) ______ can be a way of flirting or indicating that the party is only joking . A (3) ______ signifies approval, while (4) ______ of the head indicates a negative reaction. Other forms of non (5) ______ language can be found in Braille (a system of raised dots read with the fingertips), signal flags, Morse code, and smoke signals..

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. linguistic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Linguistic means relating to language or words, so non-linguistic language means communication that does not use spoken or written words. (भाषा-संबंधी)

◦ The examples given — Braille, signal flags, Morse code and smoke signals — are all systems of communication without ordinary speech, which fixes the word after “non”.

◦ Correct: Other forms of non linguistic language can be found in Braille, signal flags, Morse code, and smoke signals.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Holistic — dealing with the whole rather than the parts (समग्र); it does not contrast with words.

• Logistic — relating to the organisation and movement of resources (रसद-संबंधी); irrelevant here.

• Parodistic — relating to parody or humorous imitation; it does not describe a mode of communication.

NOTE

• Related terms: verbal (using words) vs non-verbal communication; paralinguistic features are tone, pitch and pauses.

• Braille was devised by Louis Braille (France, 1824); Morse code is named after Samuel Morse.

question: Which is the smallest planet of our solar system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mercury.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mercury is the smallest planet of the solar system, with a diameter of about 4,879 km, and it is also the planet nearest to the Sun. (बुध — सबसे छोटा ग्रह)

• It completes one revolution around the Sun in only 88 days, the shortest year of any planet, and it has no natural satellite (moon).

• Mercury has almost no atmosphere, so its surface temperature swings from about 427°C in the day to −173°C at night.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Mars (diameter ~6,792 km) is the second smallest planet and is called the Red Planet because of iron oxide on its surface.

• Venus (~12,104 km) is the hottest planet and is called Earth's twin; it rotates from east to west.

• Earth (~12,742 km) is the densest planet and the only one known to support life; Jupiter is the largest planet.

NOTE

• Order of planets from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

• Order by size (largest to smallest): Jupiter > Saturn > Uranus > Neptune > Earth > Venus > Mars > Mercury.

question: Which of the following books was written by Swami Vivekananda?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The East and the West.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The East and the West was written by Swami Vivekananda; it compares Indian and Western civilisations and culture. (पूर्व और पश्चिम)

• Swami Vivekananda (born Narendranath Datta, 12 January 1863, Kolkata) was the chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahansa.

• His other well-known works are Raja Yoga, Karma Yoga, Bhakti Yoga, Jnana Yoga, My Master and Lectures from Colombo to Almora.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• River of Smoke is a novel by Amitav Ghosh, the second book of his Ibis Trilogy (Sea of Poppies, River of Smoke, Flood of Fire).

• Ancient India is a standard history work associated with historian R. C. Majumdar, not with Vivekananda.

• Option 4 is not a work of Swami Vivekananda.

NOTE

• Vivekananda delivered his famous address at the Parliament of the World's Religions, Chicago, on 11 September 1893.

• He founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 (Belur Math, 1898); his birthday is celebrated as National Youth Day.

question: After the Battle of Plassey 1757, who from the British East India Company, became Baron of Plassey?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Robert Clive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Robert Clive commanded the English East India Company forces in the Battle of Plassey (23 June 1757), defeating Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah of Bengal. (प्लासी का युद्ध)

• The victory was won largely through the treachery of Mir Jafar, who was then made the puppet Nawab of Bengal.

• For this success Clive was raised to the peerage as Baron Clive of Plassey (1762); he became the first Governor of Bengal and introduced the Dual Government in Bengal in 1765 after the Treaty of Allahabad.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal (1773–1785) under the Regulating Act, 1773.

• John Lawrence was Viceroy of India (1864–69), known for the policy of 'masterly inactivity'.

• Charles Napier conquered Sindh in 1843 and became its first Governor.

NOTE

• The Battle of Buxar (1764) was fought by Hector Munro against Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II.

• The Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha were obtained by the Company in 1765 from Shah Alam II.

question: Ranji Trophy is affiliated with which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cricket.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ranji Trophy is India's premier first-class (domestic) cricket championship, organised by the BCCI. (रणजी ट्रॉफी — क्रिकेट)

• It began in 1934–35 and is named after K. S. Ranjitsinhji (Ranji), the Jam Saheb of Nawanagar, who played Test cricket for England.

• The first Ranji Trophy title was won by Bombay (Mumbai), which is also the most successful team with 41 titles.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other cricket tournaments: Duleep Trophy (zonal, first-class), Irani Cup, Vijay Hazare Trophy (50-over), Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (T20), Deodhar Trophy.

• Football trophies in India: Santosh Trophy, Durand Cup, Rovers Cup, Subroto Cup.

• Badminton: Thomas Cup (men), Uber Cup (women); Hockey: Agha Khan Cup, Dhyan Chand Trophy, Beighton Cup.

NOTE

• The Duleep Trophy is named after K. S. Duleepsinhji, nephew of Ranjitsinhji.

• The BCCI was founded in 1928; its headquarters is in Mumbai.

question: Which of the following is an example of a terrestrial ecosystem?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Grasslands.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A terrestrial ecosystem is a land-based ecosystem; grasslands, forests and deserts are its main types. (स्थलीय पारितंत्र)

• Grasslands are dominated by grasses and receive moderate rainfall (25–75 cm); examples include the Savanna (Africa), Prairies (North America), Steppes (Eurasia), Pampas (South America) and Velds (South Africa).

• Ponds, rivers and oceans are aquatic ecosystems, not terrestrial.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Aquatic ecosystems are of two kinds: freshwater (pond, lake, river, stream) and marine (ocean, sea, estuary).

• Ponds and lakes are examples of lentic (standing water) ecosystems, while rivers and streams are lotic (flowing water) ecosystems.

• Oceans cover about 71% of the Earth's surface and form the largest ecosystem.

NOTE

• The term 'ecosystem' was coined by A. G. Tansley (1935).

• Every ecosystem has biotic (producers, consumers, decomposers) and abiotic (light, temperature, water, soil) components.

question: Vetti tax is the most frequently mentioned tax in the inscription of Cholas who ruled in Tamil Nadu. This tax was taken in the form of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is forced labour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vetti was a tax collected by the Cholas not in cash or kind but in the form of forced (unpaid) labour. (वेट्टी — बेगार/श्रम कर)

• It is the tax most frequently mentioned in Chola inscriptions of the Tamil country.

• The other commonly mentioned Chola tax was kadamai, which was the land revenue paid by cultivators.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Chola empire was founded by Vijayalaya Chola (9th century CE); its greatest rulers were Rajaraja I (985–1014 CE) and Rajendra I (1014–1044 CE).

• The Uttaramerur inscription of Parantaka I describes the highly developed system of village self-government (sabha).

• Rajaraja I built the Brihadeeswara (Rajarajeswara) temple at Thanjavur, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• Chola village assemblies: Ur (ordinary villagers), Sabha/Mahasabha (brahmadeya villages), Nagaram (merchants).

• Rajendra I took the title Gangaikondachola after his victorious northern expedition to the Ganga.

question: In October 2022, who became the first Indian-origin Prime Minister of UK?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rishi Sunak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rishi Sunak became the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom on 25 October 2022, the first person of Indian origin and the first Hindu to hold the post. (ऋषि सुनक)

• He belongs to the Conservative Party and succeeded Liz Truss, who resigned after the shortest premiership in British history.

• Before becoming PM he served as Chancellor of the Exchequer (2020–2022); he is the son-in-law of Infosys founder N. R. Narayana Murthy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kamala Harris became the first woman Vice President of the USA in January 2021; she is of Indian-Jamaican descent.

• Neel Kashkari is an Indian-American economist and the President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis.

• Option 3 does not refer to any UK Prime Minister.

NOTE

• Other persons of Indian origin heading governments: Leo Varadkar (Ireland), Antonio Costa (Portugal), Pravind Jugnauth (Mauritius), Chandrikapersad Santokhi (Suriname).

• Rishi Sunak represents the Richmond (Yorkshire) constituency in the House of Commons.

question: Lord William Bentinck with the support of Raja Rammohan Roy abolished the practice of ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sati.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sati — the burning of a widow on her husband's funeral pyre — was declared illegal and punishable by the Bengal Sati Regulation (Regulation XVII) of 1829. (सती प्रथा)

• The regulation was passed by Governor-General Lord William Bentinck (1828–1835) with the strong support of Raja Ram Mohan Roy, founder of the Brahmo Samaj (1828).

• Bentinck also suppressed thugee (with William Sleeman) and female infanticide, and introduced English as the medium of instruction through the English Education Act, 1835 (Macaulay's Minute).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856 was passed under Lord Canning through the efforts of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.

• The Age of Consent Act, 1891 and the Sarda Act (Child Marriage Restraint Act), 1929 dealt with the marriage age of girls.

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is called the 'Father of the Indian Renaissance'; the Mughal emperor Akbar II gave him the title 'Raja'.

NOTE

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy published Sambad Kaumudi (Bengali) and Mirat-ul-Akhbar (Persian).

• Other reformers: Dayanand Saraswati (Arya Samaj, 1875), Jyotiba Phule (Satyashodhak Samaj, 1873), Annie Besant (Theosophical Society).

question: Which of the following options does NOT constitute a national income measurement method?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Credit method.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• National income is measured by only three methods — the Product (value-added) method, the Income method and the Expenditure method. (राष्ट्रीय आय मापन की विधियाँ)

• There is no 'Credit method' of measuring national income, so option 1 is the odd one out.

• All three valid methods must give the same value of national income, since production creates income which is finally spent.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Product method: sum of the gross value added by all producing units in the economy.

• Income method: sum of factor incomes — rent, wages, interest and profit.

• Expenditure method: sum of consumption + investment + government expenditure + net exports.

NOTE

• The first estimate of India's national income was made by Dadabhai Naoroji in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'; the first scientific estimate was by V. K. R. V. Rao.

• The National Income Committee (1949) was chaired by P. C. Mahalanobis; national income data is now compiled by the NSO (earlier CSO).

question: BPL is an economic benchmark related to threshold income. What does "BPL" stand for?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Below Poverty Line.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• BPL stands for Below Poverty Line, an economic benchmark used by the Government of India to identify households needing government assistance. (गरीबी रेखा से नीचे)

• The poverty line is fixed on the basis of a minimum consumption expenditure required to meet a calorie norm — 2,400 calories per day in rural areas and 2,100 calories in urban areas.

• BPL status is used for schemes such as Antyodaya Anna Yojana, PMAY, Ayushman Bharat and subsidised ration under the NFSA, 2013.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Major poverty-estimation committees: Lakdawala Committee (1993), Tendulkar Committee (2009) and Rangarajan Committee (2014).

• As per the Tendulkar Committee, about 21.9% of India's population was below the poverty line in 2011–12.

• Poverty estimates in India are based on NSSO consumption expenditure surveys.

NOTE

• NITI Aayog releases the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) based on health, education and standard of living.

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are not standard economic terms.

question: Which class of algae is commonly known as green algae?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chlorophyceae.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chlorophyceae is the class of green algae; its members contain chlorophyll a and b, which give them their grass-green colour. (हरित शैवाल)

• Their stored food is starch, and the cell wall is made of an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose.

• Common examples: Chlamydomonas, Volvox, Ulothrix, Spirogyra, Chara, Ulva.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Rhodophyceae — red algae; the red colour is due to r-phycoerythrin; stored food is floridean starch; examples: Polysiphonia, Porphyra, Gracilaria, Gelidium (source of agar).

• Phaeophyceae — brown algae; brown colour due to fucoxanthin; food stored as laminarin/mannitol; examples: Laminaria, Fucus, Sargassum, Ectocarpus.

• Desmids are a group of unicellular green algae, not a separate class of algae.

NOTE

• Algae are studied under Phycology; Fritsch classified algae into 11 classes.

• Economic uses: agar (Gelidium, Gracilaria), algin (brown algae), carrageenan (red algae), Chlorella (protein-rich food used by space travellers).

question: If the value of gross fiscal deficit will be more than net interest liabilities, the value of gross primary deficit will be ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Positive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gross Primary Deficit = Gross Fiscal Deficit − Net Interest Liabilities (interest payments). (प्राथमिक घाटा)

• If the gross fiscal deficit is greater than net interest liabilities, the difference is greater than zero, so the primary deficit is positive.

• A positive primary deficit shows that the government is borrowing not only to pay past interest but also to meet current expenditure.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• If gross fiscal deficit equals net interest liabilities, the primary deficit becomes zero; if it is less, the primary deficit is negative (primary surplus).

• Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure − Total Receipts (excluding borrowings).

• Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts; Effective Revenue Deficit = Revenue Deficit − Grants for creation of capital assets.

NOTE

• The FRBM Act, 2003 was enacted to bring fiscal discipline and reduce fiscal deficit; the N. K. Singh Committee (2017) reviewed it.

• The Union Budget is presented under Article 112 of the Constitution as the Annual Financial Statement.

question: How many General Elections to the Lok Sabha have been held till November 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 17.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Up to November 2022, a total of 17 General Elections to the Lok Sabha had been held in India. (लोकसभा आम चुनाव)

• The first General Election was held in 1951–52 and the 17th in 2019, which brought the NDA to power under Narendra Modi.

• General elections are conducted by the Election Commission of India, a constitutional body under Article 324.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Lok Sabha has a maximum strength of 550 members (530 from states + 20 from UTs); its present elected strength is 543.

• The normal term of the Lok Sabha is 5 years, extendable by one year at a time during a national emergency.

• Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India (1950–1958).

NOTE

• The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988.

• NOTA was introduced in 2013 following a Supreme Court judgment; VVPAT was first used in 2013 in Noksen (Nagaland).

question: As per census 2011, which among the following states has highest sex ratio?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meghalaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, among the given states Meghalaya has the highest sex ratio at 989 females per 1000 males. (लिंगानुपात)

• The other options are much lower — Madhya Pradesh 931, Maharashtra 929 and Uttar Pradesh 912.

• The national sex ratio in Census 2011 was 943 females per 1000 males, up from 933 in 2001.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kerala has the highest sex ratio among all states (1084) and Haryana the lowest (879).

• Among Union Territories, Puducherry had the highest (1037) and Daman & Diu the lowest (618).

• The child sex ratio (0–6 years) in 2011 was 919, the lowest since independence.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th after independence; its motto was 'Our Census, Our Future'.

• Most populous state — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim; highest literacy — Kerala (94%); lowest — Bihar (61.8%).

question: The actinides series is a group of ______ metallic chemical elements.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The actinide series consists of 15 metallic elements with atomic numbers 89 (Actinium) to 103 (Lawrencium). (एक्टिनाइड श्रेणी)

• They belong to the 5f block and, along with the lanthanides, are called inner transition elements.

• All actinides are radioactive; elements after uranium (Z > 92) are transuranic and man-made.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The lanthanide series also has 15 elements, from 57 (Lanthanum) to 71 (Lutetium), belonging to the 4f block.

• Important actinides: Thorium (90), Uranium (92), Plutonium (94), Americium (95).

• Uranium-235 is the fissile isotope used in nuclear reactors and atomic bombs.

NOTE

• The modern periodic table has 18 groups and 7 periods; the modern periodic law was given by Henry Moseley (1913).

• Lanthanides and actinides are shown separately at the bottom of the periodic table to keep it compact.

question: Gugga dance is a traditional folk dance of which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gugga (Gugga Naumi) dance is a traditional folk dance of Haryana, performed in devotion to the folk deity Gugga Pir (Gogaji), the snake god. (गुग्गा नृत्य — हरियाणा)

• It is performed during the Gugga Naumi festival in the month of Bhadrapada, when devotees carry a decorated bamboo standard called the chhari.

• Other folk dances of Haryana: Khoria, Dhamal, Phag, Loor, Ghoomar, Chhathi, Ras Leela.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kerala — Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, Theyyam, Ottamthullal, Kaikottikali.

• Assam — Bihu, Bagurumba, Jhumur, Ojapali, Sattriya (classical).

• Tamil Nadu — Bharatanatyam (classical), Karagattam, Kummi, Kolattam, Oyilattam.

NOTE

• India's eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (TN), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

• Haryana's folk songs and Saang (Swang) theatre are also popular exam topics.

question: Budhaditya Mukherjee is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sitar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Budhaditya Mukherjee is a celebrated Indian sitar player of the Imdadkhani (Etawah) gharana. (सितार वादक)

• He was trained by his father, Pandit Bimalendu Mukherjee, and is known for his mastery of both the gayaki and tantrakari styles.

• The sitar is a plucked string instrument widely used in Hindustani classical music.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other famous sitar players: Pandit Ravi Shankar, Ustad Vilayat Khan, Nikhil Banerjee, Ustad Shahid Parvez, Anoushka Shankar.

• Veena — S. Balachander, Chitti Babu, Doraiswamy Iyengar; Violin — L. Subramaniam, N. Rajam, T. N. Krishnan.

• Sarangi — Pandit Ram Narayan, Ustad Sabri Khan, Ustad Bundu Khan.

NOTE

• Instruments and exponents frequently asked: Sarod — Amjad Ali Khan, Ali Akbar Khan; Santoor — Shivkumar Sharma; Flute — Hariprasad Chaurasia; Shehnai — Bismillah Khan; Tabla — Zakir Hussain, Alla Rakha.

• Instruments are classified as tat (string), sushir (wind), avanaddha (percussion) and ghan (solid).

question: Which caves are considered as the oldest surviving rock – cut caves in India dating back to the Maurya period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Barabar and Nagarjuni caves.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Barabar and Nagarjuni caves, in the Jehanabad district of Bihar, are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, dating to the Mauryan period (3rd century BCE). (बराबर एवं नागार्जुनी गुफाएँ)

• They were excavated during the reigns of Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha, and were donated to the Ajivika sect.

• The Lomas Rishi cave is famous for its chaitya-arch facade, and the Sudama cave bears an inscription of Ashoka; the interiors have the typical Mauryan polish.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bagh Caves — Buddhist rock-cut caves in Dhar district, Madhya Pradesh, known for their mural paintings.

• Elephanta Caves — Shaivite caves on Gharapuri island near Mumbai, Maharashtra; UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); famous for the Trimurti sculpture.

• Ajanta (Buddhist, paintings) and Ellora (Buddhist, Hindu and Jain) caves are in Aurangabad, Maharashtra; both became UNESCO sites in 1983; Ellora has the rock-cut Kailasa temple built by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.

NOTE

• The Barabar caves inspired the 'Marabar Caves' of E. M. Forster's novel 'A Passage to India'.

• Other important caves: Udayagiri–Khandagiri (Odisha, Jain, King Kharavela), Karla and Bhaja (Maharashtra), Bhimbetka (MP, rock paintings).

question: Who among the following succeeded Ghatotkacha, the Gupta ruler?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandragupta I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gupta dynasty was founded by Sri Gupta, who was succeeded by Ghatotkacha, and Ghatotkacha was succeeded by his son Chandragupta I. (चंद्रगुप्त प्रथम)

• Chandragupta I (c. 319–335 CE) was the first great ruler of the dynasty and assumed the title Maharajadhiraja.

• He married the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi, and the Gupta Era (319–20 CE) is believed to have been started by him.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Samudragupta, son of Chandragupta I, is called the 'Napoleon of India' (by V. A. Smith); his achievements are recorded in the Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar Inscription) by Harisena.

• Chandragupta II 'Vikramaditya' defeated the Shakas; the Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during his reign.

• Kumaragupta I founded Nalanda University, and Skandagupta repelled the Huna invasions.

NOTE

• The Gupta age is called the 'Golden Age of India'; Kalidasa, Aryabhata, Varahamihira and Vishakhadatta belonged to this period.

• The Iron Pillar at Mehrauli (Delhi) is associated with King Chandra, generally identified with Chandragupta II.

question: Where is the Jawahar Lal Nehru Port located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Navi Mumbai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT), also known as Nhava Sheva, is located at Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, on the Arabian Sea. (जवाहरलाल नेहरू बंदरगाह)

• It was commissioned on 26 May 1989 and is the largest container port in India, handling a major share of the country's container traffic.

• Under the Major Port Authorities Act, 2021, it is now called the Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Paradip Port is in Odisha (Bhubaneswar is the state capital, not a port).

• Kolkata Port, renamed Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port, is India's only major riverine port, on the Hooghly.

• Chennai Port is an artificial harbour and one of the oldest ports on the east coast.

NOTE

• India has 12 major ports — on the west coast: Kandla (Deendayal), Mumbai, JNPA, Mormugao, New Mangalore, Cochin; on the east coast: Kolkata, Paradip, Visakhapatnam, Kamarajar (Ennore), Chennai, V. O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin).

• Vizag (Visakhapatnam) is the deepest port, and Kandla is a tidal port.

question: Teejan Bai was awarded a Padma Bhushan for her art in 2003. She is a great exponent of which dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandavani.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Teejan Bai of Chhattisgarh is the best-known exponent of Pandavani, a folk art form in which episodes of the Mahabharata are narrated with song, rhythm and dramatic movement. (पंडवानी — छत्तीसगढ़)

• The performer holds a tambura and is accompanied by a ragi; the two styles of Pandavani are Vedamati and Kapalik — Teejan Bai performs in the Kapalik style.

• She received the Padma Shri (1988), the Padma Bhushan (2003) and the Padma Vibhushan (2019), besides the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1995).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Chhau is a semi-classical masked dance of Odisha (Mayurbhanj), Jharkhand (Seraikella) and West Bengal (Purulia); it is on the UNESCO Intangible Heritage list (2010).

• Ghoomar is a famous folk dance of Rajasthan, performed by women of the Bhil and Rajput communities.

• Kalbelia is a Rajasthani snake-charmer community dance, inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010.

NOTE

• Chhattisgarh's other folk forms: Raut Nacha, Panthi, Karma, Saila, Nacha.

• Pandavani is strictly a folk singing/story-telling art; the question calls it a 'dance form', but the ticked option Pandavani is the intended and accepted answer.

question: The Zo-Mal-Lok folk dance is associated with which community?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lepcha community.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Zo-Mal-Lok is a folk dance of the Lepcha community, the earliest inhabitants of Sikkim. (लेप्चा जनजाति — सिक्किम)

• It is a harvest dance performed by young men and women in the paddy fields, imitating the movements of harvesting and threshing.

• Other Lepcha dances: Chu-Faat, Kinchum-Chu-Bomsa, Tendong Lho Rum Faat and Mon Dryak Lok.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Lushai (Mizo) community of Mizoram is known for the bamboo dance Cheraw, and for Khuallam and Chheihlam.

• The Jamatia and Chaimal are tribal communities of Tripura; Tripura's folk dances include Hojagiri (Reang), Garia, Lebang Boomani and Bizu.

• Other Sikkim dances: Singhi Chham (snow lion dance), Maruni, Tamang Selo, Yak Chham.

NOTE

• Main communities of Sikkim: Lepcha, Bhutia and Nepali.

• Sikkim became the 22nd state of India in 1975 through the 36th Constitutional Amendment Act.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the harvest festivals celebrated in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Diwali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Diwali (Deepavali) is the festival of lights, celebrated on Kartik Amavasya, marking the return of Lord Rama to Ayodhya after 14 years of exile — it is not a harvest festival. (दीपावली)

• Onam, Lohri and Baisakhi are all harvest festivals of India.

• Hence Diwali is the odd one out among the given options.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Onam — the harvest festival of Kerala (August–September), associated with the legendary king Mahabali; famous for Vallamkali (snake-boat race) and Pookalam.

• Lohri — celebrated in Punjab on 13 January, marking the end of winter and the harvesting of the rabi crop.

• Baisakhi — celebrated on 13/14 April in Punjab as a harvest festival; also marks the founding of the Khalsa Panth by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699.

NOTE

• Other harvest festivals: Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Makar Sankranti, Bihu (Assam), Nuakhai (Odisha), Wangala (Garo, Meghalaya), Ka Pomblang Nongkrem (Meghalaya).

• Diwali is celebrated by Jains as the nirvana of Mahavira and by Sikhs as Bandi Chhor Divas.

question: With respect to sports, WADA stands for ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is World Anti – Doping Agency.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• WADA stands for the World Anti-Doping Agency, the international body that promotes and coordinates the fight against doping in sports. (विश्व डोपिंग रोधी एजेंसी)

• It was founded on 10 November 1999 in Lausanne, Switzerland, and its headquarters are at Montreal, Canada.

• WADA publishes the World Anti-Doping Code and the annual List of Prohibited Substances and Methods.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India's national body is the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA), set up in 2005; the testing laboratory is the National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL), New Delhi.

• The National Anti-Doping Act, 2022 gave statutory status to NADA and the NDTL.

• Options 1, 3 and 4 are incorrect expansions of the abbreviation.

NOTE

• Other sports bodies: IOC (International Olympic Committee, 1894, Lausanne), FIFA (1904, Zurich), ICC (1909, Dubai), IAAF/World Athletics (Monaco).

• Doping means using banned performance-enhancing drugs such as anabolic steroids, stimulants and EPO.

question: Provisions related to the Panchayats are mentioned in which part of the Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part IX.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Provisions relating to Panchayats are contained in Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O) of the Constitution of India. (भाग IX — पंचायत)

• Part IX was inserted by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which came into force on 24 April 1993 (celebrated as National Panchayati Raj Day).

• The Act also added the Eleventh Schedule, containing 29 subjects transferred to the Panchayats, and provided for a three-tier system, five-year term and reservation for SC/ST and women (one-third).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Part IXA (Articles 243P–243ZG) deals with Municipalities (74th Amendment, 1992, Twelfth Schedule with 18 subjects).

• Part V deals with the Union, Part VI with the States, and Part VII (Part B States) was repealed by the 7th Amendment Act, 1956.

• Part XII deals with Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits.

NOTE

• The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended the three-tier Panchayati Raj system; Rajasthan (Nagaur, 2 October 1959) was the first state to adopt it, followed by Andhra Pradesh.

• The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) recommended a two-tier system; Article 40 (DPSP) directs the State to organise village panchayats.
